(i) the new LIVE Video Quality Database contains a collection of 150 distorted videos, obtained by four different distortion types, each of which was assessed by 15 human subjects; (ii) the database is available online, free for academic use; (iii) a statistical analysis of the performance of several publicly available algorithms was conducted; and (iv) we found that the performance of the algorithms is not as good as that of the humans.
